binders: Inherited context: q : R × R → R^m is the dependent state, with x the single spatial coordinate and t time; m is the number of components. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1).]

The flux f depends on the state q. Its role in the vector equation and its Jacobian imply a map from admissible states in R^m to R^m; a precise state domain is not specified. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9) and the flux-Jacobian sentence.]

The displayed equations concern the same state q at the same spatial and temporal arguments; (1.9) suppresses the arguments shown in (1.8). No separate quantified theorem is stated. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9).]
hypotheses: The starting differential conservation law is q_t(x,t) + ∂_x[f(q(x,t))] = 0. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8).]

Analyst inference required to interpret the rewrite classically: the relevant derivatives of q and f must exist with sufficient differentiability to apply the chain rule. The rewrite itself gives no exact regularity hypothesis. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, the rewriting sentence and (1.9); raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.2 supplies related smoothness context.]
conclusions: The conservation law (1.8) rewrites as q_t + f′(q)q_x = 0, with f′(q) the flux Jacobian evaluated at the current state. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, rewriting sentence, (1.9), and the following sentence.]

The adjacent text says this form suggests hyperbolicity if f′(q) has real eigenvalues and a corresponding set of m linearly independent eigenvectors, importing the earlier conditions on A. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, opening paragraph and paragraph following (1.9).]
definitions_and_conventions: q_t and q_x denote partial derivatives with respect to time and the single spatial coordinate. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1).]

f(q(x,t))_x is the spatial derivative of the composed flux, whereas f′(q) is the Jacobian with respect to the state variables. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9) and the phrase identifying the flux Jacobian matrix.]

The product f′(q)q_x is matrix action on a vector, inherited from the R^m-valued state and explicitly identified Jacobian matrix. The zero in the equation is consequently the zero state vector. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, state definition; raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.9) and following sentence.]

The state components represent conserved quantities; the following integral discussion interprets each component as a density. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, opening paragraph and paragraph following (1.10).]

The rewrite uses the chain-rule identity ∂_x[f(q(x,t))] = f′(q(x,t))q_x(x,t). This identity is an analyst-explicated mechanism of the displayed rewrite, not an independently numbered source claim. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9).]

The smooth differential interpretation does not establish the same rewrite for discontinuous solutions: the source expressly discusses the smoothness proviso and shocks in the ensuing subsection. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.2, opening paragraph.]

details: The two displayed expressions represent the same differential conservation law wherever the classical chain rule applies; the source presents a rewrite rather than an existence or uniqueness theorem. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, sentence linking (1.8) and (1.9).]

The flux can be nonlinear, so the matrix coefficient f′(q) can depend on the solution state. Linear flux f(q) = Aq is an included case. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, opening paragraph.]

contract_plain_english: For a state q depending on one spatial coordinate and time, the conservation law q_t + ∂_x[f(q)] = 0 is rewritten as q_t + f′(q)q_x = 0, where f′(q) is the flux Jacobian acting on the spatial derivative of the state. This is the rewrite explicitly presented in (1.8)–(1.9) on raw PDF page 25, printed page 3; its classical chain-rule regularity is implicit rather than precisely specified. The vector-valued interpretation comes from raw PDF page 23, printed page 1. The adjacent hyperbolicity observation imports the real-eigenvalue and complete-eigenvector conditions from the opening paragraph of printed page 3. The smoothness and discontinuity discussion on raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, does not license extending this classical rewrite to shock solutions without further interpretation.
